Dodge Recalls 2026 Durango SUV Over Potentially Damaged Taillight Wiring Harness Terminals
66 photos
Photo: Dodge
Stellantis North America has identified a taillight-related issue affecting only a handful of 2026 model year Durango sport utility vehicles. This campaign, which is referred to as 26V701 by the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration, is not related to the recent extended warranty coverage announcement for the rear light assembly on 2018 through 2024 models.
Older models are susceptible to water infiltration that causes the LED circuitry to corrode. Potential outcomes include dimming, partial failure, or complete light failure. Customers who paid for repairs or replacement of the taillamp assembly out of pocket can file a reimbursement claim. 2018 to 2024 Dodge Durango vehicles that have passed the five-year coverage are provided with a 6-month window from the notification date for eligible repairs.
Turning our attention back to the safety recall, which is a different animal from a customer satisfaction program that covers the rear lights, the recall documentation reveals that bent terminals in the wiring harness may be damaged. Obviously enough, such damage prevents the rear assembly from lighting up as intended, leaving following drivers to guess whether the affected vehicle is braking or not.
Subject vehicles were produced in the United States from January 5 through February 20 this year, and the Dodge brand estimates that only 3 percent of the 13,330-strong population actually contains the defect. Even so, all have to be inspected for bent terminals because reduced visibility increases the risk of a crash. Also worth noting, this defect goes against FMVSS 108.
Said federal motor vehicle safety standard requires completely functional taillamps, stop lamps, backup lamps, and turn signal lamps. Not displaying the required lighting is a noncompliance in the NHTSA's eyes, and Dodge is much obliged to please the safety boffins. The affected components are identified under two part numbers, which are supplied by Michigan's Ventra Greenwich Holdings.
Photo: Dodge 68272126AC and 68272127AC are the part numbers in question, and the Mopar eStore lists both as being compatible with 2014 through 2027 models. Unfortunately for affected customers and prospective customers, the recall documentation fails to explain what caused the terminals to bend in the first place.
Although the root cause remains a mystery for us, a clue lies in the remedy. According to Stellantis North America, dealers are to replace suspect taillamps with new units featuring "terminals with the correct dimensions." Reading between the lines, either the supplier or a sub-supplier is to blame for the potentially bent terminals.
The dealer inspection procedure, which is also available on the NHTSA 's website, tells Dodge service techs to check the production date labels on both taillamps. Anything produced from December 16, 2025, through January 27, 2026, should be considered suspect. Of course, replacement lights come at no charge to affected owners and lessees.
Stellantis North America does not describe any separate wiring harness repair in the dealer inspection procedure document. FCA US LLC's safety and regulatory team started looking into this matter back on June 16, 2026. Through September 2026, the company reviewed a bunch of records while also working with the engineering department to establish the root cause and vehicle population.
Suspect vehicles are now searchable on the NHTSA's website by VIN. Customer notification letters, however, will have to wait until December 3, 2026.
